response: Yes, size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement is an option in modern aortic surgery. This technique is used to treat ascending aortic aneurysms or dilatations, particularly in patients with connective tissue disorders or other conditions that increase the risk of aortic dilation. The procedure involves reducing the size of the aortic diameter and reinforcing it with an external wrap or mesh to prevent further dilation and reduce the risk of rupture or dissection.
